title: Sequential Grid Path Cover
summary: Given a 2D grid of size m x n with k unique values from 1 to k and the rest as 0, find a path that visits every cell exactly once and in order of the values.
statement: Given a 2D grid of size m x n with k unique values from 1 to k and the rest as 0, find a path that visits every cell exactly once and in order of the values. Return the path as a 2D array of coordinates, or an empty array if no such path exists.
constraints: The small grid contains each marker 1 through k exactly once and all other cells are zero.
Visit every cell exactly once with orthogonal moves, encountering positive markers in numerical order.
For deterministic feedback, try starts in row-major order and moves in right, down, left, up priority; return the first valid path, or an empty list.
hints: The state is the current cell, used-cell set, and next required marker; all choices must be explored because the path is Hamiltonian.
Use row-major starts and right/down/left/up neighbors so the first completion follows the deterministic app tie-break.
Enter only zero or the expected marker, advance expectation on a marker, backtrack used cells, and accept only after covering the grid.
Depth-first search follows the published priority and prunes every prefix that repeats a cell or violates marker order, so its first completion is the canonical valid path.
editorial: Depth-first search follows the published priority and prunes every prefix that repeats a cell or violates marker order, so its first completion is the canonical valid path.
